Is backup free or Premium?
Creating .fsback/.fspback backups is part of the Export & Backup toolkit, which requires Premium. Importing files (/import) works on Free, so anyone can restore a backup received from someone else.
Where should I store the backup file?
Anywhere outside Telegram: a cloud drive, your computer, or an encrypted notes app. Telegram keeps the file in your chat too, but Saved Messages is not a backup strategy.
How big is a backup file?
Small — usually kilobytes to a few megabytes, because media is referenced rather than embedded. Text and schedules compress extremely well.
Can I move my schedules to another Telegram account?
Yes. Create a backup on the old account, log into the new one, connect the channel and a sender bot, then restore the backup with Add mode. This is the standard migration path.

How Do I Delete My Fast Scheduler Account and All My Data? — Fast Scheduler Help
You can leave Fast Scheduler completely — no subscriptions to cancel by email, no dark patterns, no “are you sure” maze. One message, and everything tied to your Telegram account is erased.
How to request deletion
in Telegram and ask to delete your account. Deletion is permanent and covers
data associated with your user ID: scheduled and recurring messages, media storage, sender-bot tokens, channel connections, settings, statistics and referral records.
Export first — deletion has no undo
Before deleting, create a backup with

What happens on Telegram’s side

How long data is kept normally

While you are an active user, every category of data is kept only while it is useful: schedules until they are deleted or sent, bot tokens until you disconnect the bot, and account records until you delete the account. The Privacy Policy’s retention table lists each category with its exact lifetime.
Who do I contact to delete my Fast Scheduler account?
Message @MaximalXP on Telegram and request account deletion. The deletion is permanent and removes all data linked to your Telegram ID.
Can I delete everything but keep the bot?
Yes — you can delete individual schedules, media and sender bots from inside the bot without deleting your account. Full deletion is only for leaving the service entirely.
Should I export a backup before deleting?
Definitely. After deletion there is no way to restore anything, so create a backup with /backup first if there is any chance you will return.
Why Is My Telegram Channel Posting Twice? (Duplicate Posts, Explained) — Fast Scheduler Help
Why Is My Telegram Channel Posting Twice? (Duplicate Posts, Explained)
Double posts are annoying for subscribers and make a channel look automated in the worst way. The good news: the cause is nearly always one of four things.
1. Another account still schedules the channel
The most common cause after a migration or team handover: the old account's schedules were never removed. Both accounts happily queue posts for the same time. Fix: in the
other
account, open
and delete its schedules (or disconnect the channel). If you cannot access the old account, remove the bot from the channel's admin list — that stops the posting immediately.
2. Two sender bots are admin in the channel

Every channel must pair with exactly one sender bot, and that bot should be the only bot with posting rights. If you created a second bot and added it as admin, posts may arrive from both. Keep one sender bot per channel as admin; remove extra bots from the channel.
3. The message got scheduled twice
Easy to do when re-sending the same text after an edit, or when importing while old schedules exist. Open the Message List for the day and scan for same-time twins before the posting window. The
view makes clusters obvious.
4. The recurrence rule was duplicated, not edited
Creating a new daily rule instead of editing the existing one produces two identical posts every day. Check the recurring list — if two rules share the same text and time, delete one.
Still posting twice?
to see what is queued, then use
with the channel name and two timestamps of a duplicate pair. Support can trace which connection produced each post.
Does Fast Scheduler retry a post that failed, causing doubles?
A retry only happens when the send did not confirm. If Telegram accepted the post but the confirmation was lost (rare network hiccup), you can get one duplicate. It does not re-send confirmed posts.
Can I merge two accounts scheduling the same channel?
Yes — export from the old account, import with Add on the new one, then clear the old account. Never leave both active.

Can I Edit a Scheduled Post After Scheduling It? — Fast Scheduler Help
Can I Edit a Scheduled Post After Scheduling It?
Nothing about a scheduled post is carved in stone. Until the moment Telegram accepts the send, every part of it can change — that is the whole point of keeping a queue instead of posting immediately.
What you can change
Text and formatting
— fix a typo, rewrite the hook, add links. Bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, spoilers and code all survive edits.
— swap the image, replace the video, add or remove an album item.
Send time
— move the post earlier or later, or to another day entirely.
Target channel
— re-point a post to a different connected channel.
Open the
), tap the post, choose
🔄 Replace
. The familiar schedule flow reopens with the post's current content pre-filled — change what you need and confirm.
What editing cannot do
Change a post that already published.
Once the sender bot delivers the message to Telegram, it is a normal Telegram message — edit it with Telegram's own tools, not here.
Edit recurring posts “in place”.
A recurring rule is a single template that fires on its pattern — there are no separate per-day copies. Edit the
rule
so all future sends change.
A workflow that actually works

Channel operators who stay sane usually: schedule the week on Sunday, review the Calendar Monday, and treat edit as the normal verb — improving copy as the news moves. Edits are free, instant, and never notify subscribers. The only deadline is the send time itself.
How late can I edit a post?
Any time before the send moment. If the bot is mid-delivery, the edit may not apply — that is the only race. For a post due within seconds, delete and reschedule instead.
Can I edit a post that already went out?
Not from the bot — it is a regular Telegram message now. Telegram itself lets admins edit posted messages in channels; use Telegram for that.
Does editing reset the monthly send counter?
No. The counter counts actual sends, not edits. Editing costs nothing.

How Do I Format Telegram Posts? (Bold, Italic, Links, Spoilers and Buttons) — Fast Scheduler Help
Formatting is what separates a channel that looks professional from one that looks like a group chat. Fast Scheduler keeps every bit of it intact between scheduling and publishing.
Rich text survives the whole pipeline
Write a message anywhere — bold headlines, italic asides,
underlined

struck-through
corrections, monospace code — and schedule it. Formatting is stored as Telegram
entities

Wrap part of the text in spoiler markup and it publishes as a real Telegram spoiler — blurred until a reader taps it. Perfect for giveaways, answers, and sensitive details. The bot validates spoiler markup while you type, so unclosed pairs are caught at scheduling time, not in front of your audience.
Inline URL buttons
Add tappable buttons to any post with one syntax:
[Button Text](https://example.com)

. Use them for call-to-action links — “Read the guide”, “Buy now”, “Join the chat”. Buttons attach to text posts and to media posts alike. Keep button labels short (two or three words read best) and test one post before scheduling a whole campaign.
Premium Telegram emoji in your drafts are preserved on publish, so your brand’s custom smileys do not degrade into defaults.
Signatures: formatting that stamps itself
Configure a

once — a footer with your links, hashtags or contact — and every scheduled post carries it automatically, on text and media alike. Signatures keep their own formatting, and you can override the signature per post when a particular message should go out clean.
A checklist for polished posts
One bold hook line first — most readers see only it in notifications.
Links as buttons where possible; they out-click inline links.
Spoilers for anything the reader should opt into.
A signature so every post quietly advertises your next channel.
Does Telegram formatting survive scheduling in Fast Scheduler?
Yes. Bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, code, links, spoilers and custom emoji are stored as Telegram entities and publish exactly as written.
How do I add buttons to a scheduled Telegram post?
Use the syntax [Button Text](https://your-link.com) in the message. The bot converts it into a tappable inline URL button on the published post.

Yes. Create a signature once and it is appended to every scheduled and recurring post automatically, keeping its own formatting. Individual posts can override it.

Do unused sends carry over to next month?

Both formats package your selected data — scheduled messages, recurring messages, settings, and more — into one archive you can download, store in the cloud, or move to another account. Media you saved in Media Storage is referenced, not re-uploaded, so files stay small.
Which one should you pick?

Is .fspback more secure than .fsback?
Yes. A .fspback file is encrypted with the password you set; a .fsback file is not protected at all. If the backup contains bot tokens or private content, prefer .fspback.
I lost the password to my .fspback file. Can it be recovered?
No. The password cannot be reset or bypassed — not even by support. Keep the password (and the hint you optionally set) together with the file. Without it the backup is unreadable.
Can I convert .fsback to .fspback (or back)?
Indirectly: restore the .fsback file into your account, then create a new backup and choose password protection to get a .fspback file. There is no direct file-conversion command.
Which formats can I import besides these?
Imports also accept .json, .csv, .txt, .rtf and .odt files (and SetDate bundles). Those carry messages only, while .fsback/.fspback carry your full configuration.
What Is Media Storage and How Do You Use It Without Losing Your Mind? — Fast Scheduler Help
What Is Media Storage and How Do You Use It Without Losing Your Mind?

Media Storage is your in-bot asset library: save a photo, video, or document once, then reuse it in any scheduled post without re-uploading. If you repost evergreen content or reuse brand imagery, this is the feature that saves the most time per week.
Boxes: folders with a purpose
Assets live in
— named containers like “Brand”, “Memes”, “Product shots”. Free gets
1 box with 100 items
(no video in storage); Premium gets
20 boxes × 500 items
with video support. Boxes keep the picker fast and your library mentally organized — one box per campaign is a good default.
Saving and reusing
Save:
forward or upload media to the storage, or save straight from a scheduled message you are composing.
Reuse:
while scheduling, open the storage instead of attaching a file — pick the asset, done. Telegram file references are reused, so nothing is re-uploaded and quality is not recompressed per post.
Organize:
move items between boxes, rename, delete.
The limits that actually matter
Item count
— the 100-item Free box fills fast with albums; delete stale assets or upgrade.
Video on Free
— storage refuses video on Free; schedule videos directly instead, or move to Premium for video-in-storage.
Size
— same upload caps as messages: 10 MB on Free, 100 MB on Premium.
A cleanup cadence that works
Once a month: open each box, delete anything unused in 60 days, archive campaign boxes by renaming with a date prefix. Two minutes, and the picker stays a joy instead of an archaeology dig.
Does deleting a media item break scheduled posts using it?
Posts keep working — a scheduled message holds its own reference to the media. Deleting from storage only removes it from the library for future posts.
Can I share a box with another admin?
Storage is per account. To share assets, export them as part of a backup or send the files directly — the other account saves them into their own storage.

Scheduled Message Didn’t Post? The 6 Real Causes, In Order of Likelihood — Fast Scheduler Help
When a post misses its slot, the cause is almost always in the delivery chain — the schedule itself is the least likely suspect. Work this list top to bottom; each item fixes the majority of cases.
1. The sender bot lost its admin seat
Someone cleaned up admins and removed your sender bot. Check
Manage Channel → Administrators
: your sender bot must be there with
. Re-add it, and the queue resumes.
2. The token was revoked or replaced
in @BotFather kills the old token everywhere instantly. If the bot shows the sender as disconnected, open
under the bot and paste the fresh token.
3. Permissions were narrowed
Admin exists but without
— a silent killer after permission tightening. Open the admin entry and re-enable posting.
4. The channel changed identity
Username changed or the channel was converted — the old link no longer resolves. Reconnect the channel; schedules are kept.
5. Telegram rate limits on bursts

Telegram throttles aggressive posting bursts channel-wide. If several posts fire close together and one fails, it is usually this. Space posts by minutes, not seconds — the scheduler already does, but third-party bots added to the channel can collide with it.
6. The monthly send cap (Free)
On Free, sends pause at 100 per channel per month until the 1st. The bot warns you before the cap;
shows the counter. Premium lifts the cap entirely.
Fastest diagnosis
(status of everything) and check the sender-bot status screen. Still mysterious?
with the channel and the missed time — support can see delivery attempts and will tell you exactly which step failed.
Will missed posts send later automatically?
A post that failed delivery is marked failed, not silently retried forever. Fix the underlying cause, then delete it and schedule it again.
How do I know if it was the monthly cap?
The bot notifies you at the cap, and /stats shows monthly usage per channel. If neither shows the cap, it was delivery-side — start the checklist from the top.

inside

Four ways to connect the channel

Can Fast Scheduler post to a private channel?

Does the sender bot also need admin rights in a private channel?
Yes. The main bot needs Post Messages to verify and manage, and your sender bot needs Post Messages because it is the account that actually publishes every scheduled post.
How many channels can I connect on the Free plan?
Free includes 1 channel with 100 sent messages per month. Premium raises the limit to 3 channels with unlimited sends.
